claim: Fannjiang & Listgarten (NeurIPS 2020) formalize the exact same core mechanism the audited paper claims as its diagnosis -- that a surrogate/oracle becomes exploitable as the search distribution departs the training distribution -- via a non-zero-sum game between the search distribution p_theta(x) and the oracle parameters beta, four years before the audited paper.
stance_target: Whether the audited paper's 'core diagnosis' (which off-distribution maximizers a surrogate's mean admits) has prior articulation in offline design literature
quoted_support: "oracle-based design is distinguished by the fact that it seeks solutions -- and therefore, will query the oracle -- in regions of the design space that are not well-represented by the oracle training data... a major challenge arises when an oracle is employed for design: its outputs, including its uncertainty estimates, become unreliable beyond the training data."

claim: Fannjiang & Listgarten explicitly attribute the sub-optimality of oracle-based design to 'pathological behavior of the oracle when the search model, p_theta(x), strays too far from the training distribution during the optimization' -- naming the distributional-departure-causes-oracle-exploitation mechanism directly.
stance_target: Prior articulation of surrogate exploitation as a function of distributional departure in offline/oracle-based design
scope_conditions: Section 3, formalization of model-based design as a non-zero-sum game
quoted_support: "the solution to the oracle-based problem will, in general, be sub-optimal with respect to the original objective that uses the ground truth... This sub-optimality can be extreme due to pathological behavior of the oracle when the search model, p_theta(x), strays too far from the training distribution during the optimization."

claim: Fannjiang & Listgarten's proposed fix (autofocusing: iteratively retraining the oracle toward a Nash equilibrium as the design distribution shifts) treats distributional distance/staleness as the primary driver of oracle unreliability, an implicit premise that the audited paper's Elimination 7 complicates by showing distance predicts aggregate loss but does not discriminate between surrogate classes at matched distance.
stance_target: Whether the audited paper's Elimination-7 finding is a refinement of, rather than a restatement of, Fannjiang & Listgarten's distance-centric diagnosis
scope_conditions: Comparison between Fannjiang's autofocusing premise and the audited paper's per-optimum distance/inflation instrumentation across 5,040 optima
quoted_support: Fannjiang: "successful oracle-based design thus involves an inherent trade-off between the need to stay 'near' the training data in order to trust the oracle, and the need to depart from it in order to make improvements." Audited paper: "across 5,040 optima, distance predicts both over-prediction (rho=+0.758) and true loss (rho=-0.818)... but it does not discriminate: the classes sit at the same median distance (0.87 against 0.86) and differ in outcome anyway."

claim: Fannjiang & Listgarten do not run any crossed surrogate-class x optimizer-class comparison, do not use ANOVA/factorial/variance-decomposition machinery, and do not distinguish between GP-family and ensemble-family surrogates as classes with differential off-distribution behavior -- so the paper cannot itself satisfy or threaten the audited paper's N6 claim.
stance_target: Whether fannjiang2020autofocused constitutes a kill of N6
quoted_support: Zero hits for 'maximizer', 'exploit', 'distribution shift', 'off-distribution' as literal strings; the paper's own vocabulary is 'oracle gap', 'non-zero-sum game', and 'autofocusing' rather than the audited paper's 'off-distribution maximizer admission' framing

claim: The audited paper never cites fannjiang2020autofocused anywhere in its related-work discussion of oracle exploitation, distributional shift, or offline design (checked against main.tex), despite the paper being the founding formalization of the oracle-exploitation-under-distributional-shift problem the audited paper's core diagnosis restates.
stance_target: Completeness of the audited paper's related-work coverage for its central diagnostic claim
quoted_support: Zero matches for 'fannjiang', 'autofocus', 'Fannjiang', 'brookes' distribution-shift framing, or 'oracle gap' anywhere in main.tex; fannjiang2020autofocused appears only in references.bib (never \cite'd)
